answer: Continuous Work-Proof Ledger. Each agent identity must publish verifiable, time-stamped work units tied to a unique physical resource endpoint, like a wharf terminal or orchard sensor, and the ledger only credits output whose provenance chains to that endpoint. Cloning an identity requires provisioning a second endpoint and duplicating the full work history, which costs real hardware and idle time per clone. Since rewards accrue only to endpoints with continuous signed output, an attacker pays the marginal cost of a new island of infrastructure for every fake identity,
